item.title: Xenophobic attacks: Help South Africans, don’t punish them — OAU don
item.description: …As varsity’s International Relations Department marks 50th anniversary By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo The Federal Government has been urged to adopt a sympathetic approach towards South Africa over the recent xenophobic attacks, rather than resort to punitive measures, with a don at the Obafemi Awolowo University (OAU), Ile-Ife, saying South Africans need help at a difficult time. A Professor of International Relations at OAU, Charles Ukeje, said the xenophobic violence was regrettable, particularly given Nigeria’s significant contributions, alongside other African countries, to the struggle against apartheid in South Africa. Ukeje spoke during a press conference organised to herald the 50th anniversary of the university’s Department of International Relations at the campus. He blamed the attacks partly on the failure of successive South African governments to adequately educate their citizens about the sacrifices made by Nigeria and other African countries towards ending apartheid. According to him, proper education about the contributions of other African nations could have helped foster a stronger sense of brotherhood among South Africans and other Africans. He said: “I believe that the xenophobic violence in South Africa is very regrettable. It is regrettable because this is a country which the rest of the continent, particularly Nigeria, helped to midwife in the context of apartheid. “So, in the post-apartheid era, you would expect that the South Africans will be more and better disposed to the rest of Africans, given the amount of sacrifice that Nigerians and other African countries have made in the bid to end apartheid in that country. “It is regrettable that generations of South African leaders, upon achieving an end to apartheid, really did not adequately educate their citizens on the role the whole of Africa played. “Perhaps, if they had done that, things would have been different. Perhaps, the ordinary South African citizens on the street would treat and see other Africans as brothers.” On Nigeria’s response, the don said the country should maintain its longstanding commitment to Africa as the centrepiece of its foreign policy. He urged the Federal Government to demonstrate leadership by showing understanding towards South Africa, despite the hostility some of its citizens might harbour towards Nigerians. “In terms of how Nigeria should respond, Africa has always been the centrepiece of Nigeria’s foreign policy. I don’t think that is going to change. “I think Nigeria has the responsibility to continue to see itself as a leader on the continent. I think that role for Nigeria is perhaps more important today than it was anytime. “And I’m looking forward to the Nigerian government not really wielding the big stick against South Africa, but to actually acknowledge that the country and its citizens are facing very difficult circumstances at this time and we need to be more sympathetic to them, even with the amount of disdain that the ordinary ci

item.title: Lagos govt warns PSPs over refuse crisis, demands results
item.description: …..As Solus, Olusosun dumpsites resume operations …PSPs to deploy over 700 trucks By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Government has warned Private Sector Participation (PSP) waste operators to deliver immediate results or face enforcement measures, following the reopening of the Solus and Olusosun dumpsites after months of closure. The government said it had fulfilled its responsibility by rehabilitating the facilities and their access roads, leaving waste operators with no further excuses for the persistent refuse crisis across the state. Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Tokunbo Wahab, gave the warning on Wednesday during an inspection of the previously closed Solus dumpsite in Alimosho Local Government Area. Wahab said the government expected PSP operators to improve waste collection and evacuation across their areas of operation, stressing that residents deserved value for the services they paid for. “Too much is given, so much more is expected. There are no more excuses,” the commissioner said, recounting his message to the leadership of the PSP operators. “The state government has done its own bit; let your PSP members also put their skin in it and see how they can achieve what we set out jointly to achieve because they suggested we put this into play and now we’ve done it for them.” According to him, the decision to reopen Solus followed proposals by waste operators to rehabilitate the facility rather than wait for the development of new dumpsites around Badagry and Epe. He explained that Solus, located within Lagos West, serves several local government areas, including Alimosho, Ajeromi-Ifelodun, Mushin, Badagry, Ikeja, Ojo and Apapa. The commissioner said the contractor handling the rehabilitation had assured the government that the repaired access road would last at least one year, subject to quarterly maintenance. He added that the facility was expected to accommodate at least 100 trucks daily, significantly improving waste evacuation in the affected areas. “100 trucks from this axis coming here to discharge gives us the comfort that our streets, our homes will not be littered with waste,” Wahab said. Addressing complaints by residents over the failure of some PSP operators to collect refuse regularly, the commissioner said the state government would enforce its polluter-pays policy to ensure operators delivered the services for which residents paid. He warned that the government would take necessary measures to hold defaulting operators accountable. LAWMA restructuring Wahab also confirmed a major restructuring of the Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA), ordered by the state governor, as part of efforts to improve waste management operations. He announced the appointment of Juwon Akinyemi as Acting Managing Director, Dr Tjani Olorunwa as Acting Executive Director of Operations, and Kunle Adebiyi as substantive Executive Director of Finance. item.title: ADC protesters take Mark judgment dispute to NJC, UN, EU, UK, US embassies
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — Members of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) on Wednesday staged a protest at the Federal High Court in Abuja, demanding the release of the Certified True Copy (CTC) of the judgment nullifying the party’s National Working Committee led by former Senate President, David Mark. The protesters accused the trial judge, Justice Peter Lifu, of withholding the November 5 judgment despite an application by the party’s lawyers and payment of the prescribed fees, arguing that the delay was frustrating their efforts to challenge the ruling at the Court of Appeal. The protesters also extended their campaign beyond the court premises, storming the headquarters of the United Nations (UN), as well as the European Union (EU), United Kingdom and United States embassies in Abuja, where they submitted letters seeking diplomatic attention and support for what they described as due process, the right of appeal and credible elections in Nigeria. The letters bore the subject: “Urgent Appeal for Diplomatic Attention and Support for Due Process, the Right of Appeal and Credible Elections in Nigeria – Re: Judgment Delivered on 5th November, 2026 in Suit No: FHC/ABJ/CS/1819/2025 (Nafiu Bala Gombe Vs. ADC & Ors).” Speaking during the protest, a former Acting Chairman of the ADC in the Federal Capital Territory, Yusuf Shehu Tijani, described the judgment as a sham and called on the National Judicial Council (NJC) to intervene. “Our reason for coming here today is what Justice Lifu is doing. He is holding on to the sham judgment he said he passed. He should send the CTC, so that we can get it and appeal the judgment. “Moreover, the Supreme Court already affirmed the leadership of Senator David Mark as the National Chairman of the African Democratic Congress. So why is the High Court going against that recognition, saying he’s passing a judgment? “Now the judgment you passed, give us the Certified True Copy so that we can appeal. He is refusing to do that. That is why we are here,” Tijani said. He said the protest was intended to draw the NJC’s attention to the alleged delay and compel the judge to release the document. “So the protest is to call on the NJC to pressure this man, let him do what is right, because justice must prevail in Nigeria. This is not a jungle. This is a country that has laws, that has rules, and we have to follow the Constitution of the country. “The stated law is that he should send the CTC so that we can appeal the judgment, which is a sham judgment in the first place,” he added. The protest followed a November 10 petition addressed to the Chief Judge of the Federal High Court, Justice John Tsoho, by members of the ADC candidates’ forum, demanding the immediate release of the judgment. item.title: Police probe Blord over armed officers’ escort
item.description: The Nigeria Police Force has launched an investigation into a viral video showing armed police officers escorting businessman Linus Williams, popularly known as Blord, at the Akanu Ibiam International Airport, Enugu. The Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Ani Iniedu, described the deployment of the officers as “unlawful and illegal”, saying an investigation had commenced into the incident. Iniedu disclosed this in a statement posted on his official X account on Wednesday while reacting to the video. “Unlawful and illegal. Investigation has commenced into this incident please. We say #notoimpunity,” he wrote. The video, which Blord shared on his Instagram page on Tuesday, showed him arriving at the Akanu Ibiam International Airport in Enugu, accompanied by armed police officers dressed in camouflage uniforms and tactical gear. The businessman was seen wearing a red-and-white striped traditional cap associated with the Kwankwaso political brand. He was also seen arriving in a black Cadillac with the personalised number plate, “B-LORD”. Other scenes in the footage showed Blord walking alongside the armed officers at the airport and at other locations, including what appeared to be his business premises. The officers were seen providing him with an escort and opening the vehicle door for him. Captioning the video, Blord wrote: “Back to base, business as usual. From the airport to a brief stop at BlordGroup Enugu branch, then back to Awka. Every move has its purpose, and the vision never takes a break. Blord is home!” In another Instagram post, the businessman said he had been in Sabon Gari, Kano State, where he met his “brothers” before returning to Enugu. The development comes months after President Bola Tinubu ordered the withdrawal of police officers attached to Very Important Persons (VIPs) across the country and their redeployment to core policing duties. Tinubu gave the directive at a security meeting with service chiefs and the Director-General of the Department of State Services in Abuja on November 23, 2025. According to a statement by the President’s Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, VIPs requiring protection would henceforth be assigned armed operatives of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps instead of police officers. The President said the measure was aimed at strengthening police presence in communities, particularly those facing security challenges. On December 6, 2025, the police also deployed a Special Enforcement Team to monitor compliance with the directive, beginning with an operation in Lagos. The then Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Benjamin Hundeyin, said the exercise recorded no cases of unauthorised deployment of police escorts. item.description: Troops of the Nigerian Army have apprehended two suspected terrorists (father and son) in Sokoto State. The suspects, identified as Muhammadu Ali and his son, Umaru Ali, were arrested at Bauni Forest in Tangaza Local Government Area. The operational report made available to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Wednesday said the operation was conducted by troops of 248 Battalion, supported by the French Special Forces and the NCTC-Office of the National Security Adviser tactical team. The report said the suspects were apprehended at about 10:00 a.m. on Wednesday and were believed to be from the Bauni village area. According to the report, items recovered during the operation included one AK-47 rifle, one magazine containing three rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition, ₦9,760 and three motorcycle tubes. The report said the suspects were in the custody of 8 Military Intelligence Battalions for further investigation. item.title: Oil resumption agreement must benefit Ogonis, be enforceable — KAGOTE
item.description: …Recommends Ogoni development plan, seeks stronger HYPREP By Daniel Abia P/HARCOURT — The leadership of KAGOTE, the apex socio-cultural organisation of the Ogoni people, has said any memorandum of understanding (MoU) between the Federal Government and the Ogoni people on the resumption of oil exploration must be comprehensive, credible, enforceable and beneficial to the people. The organisation said the agreement must enjoy the confidence and support of the Ogoni people and remain beneficial to generations yet unborn. KAGOTE stated this on Tuesday during this year’s remembrance of the Ogoni Nine in Port Harcourt. In his address at the event, the President of KAGOTE, Chief Lesi Maol, said the proposed agreement should be a historic document that future generations would read with pride and gratitude. He said it should have the enduring significance of the Ogoni Bill of Rights and reflect the wisdom and commitment of those negotiating on behalf of the people. Maol said: “We should aspire to produce an agreement whose significance and enduring value can stand alongside the Ogoni Bill of Rights as another defining milestone in our history. “An agreement of such historic significance must not be judged by the speed with which it is concluded, the prominence of those who sign it or the ceremonies that accompany it. It must be judged by its content, its fairness, its enforceability and the measurable benefits it secures for our people. “We must move beyond promises that are difficult to measure and commitments that future generations may struggle to enforce. Let us negotiate an agreement that will outlive its signatories, survive changes in leadership and remain beneficial to Ogoniland long after those of us gathered here today have departed. That is the standard our history demands of us.” He acknowledged progress in the ongoing dialogue with the Federal Government but stressed that the credibility of the negotiation process was as important as its outcome. While welcoming the government’s recognition of confidence-building measures, Maol said such measures should be substantially implemented with visible and verifiable results before any final MoU was concluded. He said the measures should address the concerns of the Ogoni people, demonstrate good faith and provide the necessary assurance for meaningful negotiations. To achieve this, he called for credible, transparent and inclusive congresses across the four Ogoni local government areas of Khana, Gokana, Tai and Eleme. According to him, the congresses should provide opportunities for communities, traditional institutions, women, youths, professionals and other recognised stakeholders to express their expectations and determine priorities for the negotiations. He further proposed that a competent and representative negotiating team, backed by independent legal, environmental, technical and financial experts, should conduct the negotiations based on the mandate emerging from the congresses. item.title: Abia first in S’East to implement CONLESS for Assembly workers
item.description: . Otti approves 25% salary increase, implementation begins January By Steve Oko Abia State has become the first state in the South-East to adopt the Consolidated Legislative Salary Structure (CONLESS) for parliamentary workers, with Governor Alex Otti approving a 25 per cent salary increase for eligible staff. The new salary structure, which covers employees of the Abia State House of Assembly and the House of Assembly Service Commission, will take effect from January 2027. The Chief Press Secretary to the Governor, Njoku Ukoha, disclosed this in a statement on Wednesday, saying the approval followed recommendations by the committee set up to work out the implementation of CONLESS. CONLESS is the approved remuneration structure for legislative workers in the National Assembly, state Houses of Assembly and their respective service commissions. Its implementation has remained outstanding in several states despite persistent demands by parliamentary workers. The approval is expected to address disparities in the remuneration of legislative staff, improve their welfare and strengthen the institutional capacity of the legislature. The development also marks a significant step in Abia’s efforts to improve public sector remuneration and promote fairness in the state’s workforce. item.title: Nigerian pilgrims visit fortress where John the Baptist was martyred, pray for Nigeria
item.description: By Jimoh Babatunde More than 40 Nigerian Christian pilgrims led by Aeroport Travels & Tours Ltd. have visited Mukawir, an ancient fortress in Jordan associated with the imprisonment and execution of John the Baptist, offering prayers for courage, steadfast faith and righteous leadership in Nigeria. The delegation, led by Dr Oludayo Taiwo Gideon, Group Managing Director of Aeroport Group, arrived at Queen Alia International Airport, Amman, in the early hours of Tuesday after departing Lagos on Monday. The pilgrims visited Mukawir following an earlier excursion to Mount Nebo, combining spiritual reflection with historical and cultural tourism. Mukawir, historically known as Machaerus, is traditionally identified as the location where John the Baptist was imprisoned and executed under Herod Antipas, as recounted in the biblical books of Matthew 14 and Mark 6. Speaking at the historic site, Gideon said the visit was deliberately included in the pilgrimage itinerary to remind participants of the courage and unwavering conviction required to uphold their faith. He said the pilgrims prayed for spiritual strength, steadfast faith, divine protection and the grace to remain committed to their Christian beliefs despite life’s challenges. “John the Baptist did not compromise the truth, even when it cost him his life. At Mukawir, we prayed for spiritual strength, for steadfast faith, for divine protection, and for the grace to remain committed to our Christian beliefs despite life’s challenges. We also prayed for Nigeria, for righteous leadership, for justice, for peace, and for divine intervention in the affairs of our country,” he said. The prayers also focused on families, national peace, justice and the need for leaders committed to integrity and good governance. Describing Mukawir as a place of sober reflection, Gideon said the experience held important lessons for Nigeria, particularly the need for citizens and leaders to stand for truth and righteousness without fear or favour. “Nigeria needs men and women like John, who will speak truth, stand for righteousness, and not bow to fear or favour. That was our prayer for our nation,” he added. He noted that visits to biblical locations enabled pilgrims to appreciate the geographical and historical settings of events recorded in the Scriptures and translate their lessons into personal and collective spiritual commitments. The delegation also visited a mosaic museum and an artefact shop, where members explored Jordan’s artistic and cultural heritage, including its traditional mosaic craftsmanship, while purchasing locally made souvenirs and other items. Gideon said the cultural excursion demonstrated the economic and heritage-preservation opportunities associated with religious pilgrimage beyond visits to sacred sites. “Pilgrimage is not only spiritual, it is also cultural and economic. item.title: Dalung accuses ADC of risking 2027 election participation
item.description: ….Faults Aregbesola over caretaker committee appointments Solomon Dalung, a chieftain of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), has accused the party’s National Secretary, Rauf Aregbesola, of unilaterally appointing caretaker committees across the states, warning that the move could undermine the party’s pending case before the Supreme Court and jeopardise its participation in the 2027 elections. The former Minister of Youth and Sports Development made the allegations in a video posted on his Facebook page on Tuesday. He alleged that appointment letters purportedly signed by Aregbesola had been circulated to members of the caretaker committees to manage the party’s affairs across the country. Dalung expressed concern that the party was taking decisions capable of worsening its legal challenges despite a pending appeal before the Supreme Court. “This evening, I bring a strong-worded message to the leadership of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Nigeria. It seems that the party has not learned any lesson from the plethora of litigations confronting it,” he said. “We woke up this morning with social media inundated with letters of appointment of caretaker committee members for the 36 states, signed by the national secretary of the party.” He alleged that the appointments involved individuals removed from office by the Court of Appeal, adding that their challenge against the decisions remained pending before the apex court. Describing the action as a disregard for due process, Dalung accused the party leadership of attempting to pre-empt the Supreme Court’s decision. “This action of the party is intended to undermine the integrity of the judiciary and pre-empt the decision on the matter before your lordships at the Supreme Court,” he said. “This act is unacceptable to right-thinking Nigerians and lovers of the principles of the rule of law and democracy. And as a minister in the temple of justice and a barrister of the Supreme Court, I will not stand with the ADC to undermine the judicial process.” He urged the party to suspend the planned inauguration of the caretaker committees, scheduled for Wednesday, pending the determination of the appeal by the Supreme Court. Dalung warned that proceeding with the inauguration could weaken the party’s legal position and threaten its participation in the 2027 general election. “Should the party proceed to inaugurate these persons, the consequences are obvious. It means the ADC is not committed to participating in the 2027 elections,” he said. “The ADC cannot approach the Supreme Court to challenge the decision of the Court of Appeal, which affirmed the removal of these persons following the state congresses and national convention, and then turn around, while the appeal is pending, to invite the same persons and inaugurate them as chairmen of caretaker committees.” Questions Aregbesola’s authority Dalung also questioned why Aregbesola alone signed the appointment letters, arguing that the party’s adminis

item.title: Otti approves 25% salary increase for Assembly workers
item.description: …FENRAD urges gov to extend salary review to other workers By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — The Foundation for Environmental Rights Advocacy and Development (FENRAD) has urged Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, to extend the salary improvement approved for legislative workers to other categories of public servants, including teachers, healthcare professionals and local government employees. The call followed the governor’s approval of a 25 per cent implementation of the Consolidated Legislative Salary Structure (CONLESS) for eligible workers of the Abia State House of Assembly and the Assembly Service Commission. The new salary structure, which takes effect from January 2027, reportedly makes Abia the first state in the South-East to adopt CONLESS for parliamentary workers. The Chief Press Secretary to the Governor, Njoku Ukoha, disclosed the approval in a statement on Wednesday, saying it followed recommendations by a committee set up to work out the implementation of the salary structure. CONLESS is the approved remuneration framework for legislative workers in the National Assembly, state Houses of Assembly and their respective service commissions. Its implementation has remained outstanding in several states despite demands by parliamentary workers. Reacting in a statement on Wednesday, FENRAD’s Executive Director, Comrade Nelson Nnanna Nwafor, commended Otti for the approval, describing it as a step towards improving workers’ welfare, addressing remuneration disparities and strengthening legislative administration. He, however, urged the state government to adopt an inclusive approach to workers’ welfare by extending comparable salary improvement measures to other Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs). According to him, teachers, healthcare workers, local government employees, administrative personnel and other public servants also deserve improved remuneration, decent working conditions and institutional support. While acknowledging the distinct remuneration framework for legislative workers, Nwafor said its implementation should not exclude other categories of public servants from government efforts to improve their welfare. FENRAD also called for transparent implementation of the approved 25 per cent adjustment from January 2027, adequate budgetary provisions, periodic salary reviews and regular engagement with organised labour and civil society groups. The organisation said good governance should be measured not only by infrastructure development and policy announcements but also by the extent to which government decisions improve workers’ living conditions, dignity and economic security. item.title: Kwankwaso and I have failed if anyone remains in IDP camps after 18 months — Obi
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has promised to tackle Nigeria’s displacement crisis, declaring that his administration would have failed if any Nigerian remained in an Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) camp 18 months after assuming office. Obi gave the assurance while speaking in Jos, the Plateau State capital, on Wednesday, where he pledged to prioritise national unity and security if elected president in the 2027 general election. He lamented the divisions among Nigerians along ethnic and religious lines, insisting that national unity was essential to addressing the country’s challenges. According to him, his administration would focus on uniting the country and ensuring the safety of citizens, particularly in communities affected by persistent killings and displacement. “Our commitment is to unite Nigeria because today there is no unity, we are divided along tribal lines, religious lines, and that should not be, we are Nigerians. “Number two is to secure Nigeria. It’s our priority to ensure that Nigerians live in safety. In a place like Plateau and Benue where people are being killed daily, I assure you that no mother will cry again for her children. I assure you that no woman will feel the pain of losing a husband, neither will the father feel the pain of losing a wife,” he said. The former Anambra State governor stressed that his administration would not tolerate a situation in which Nigerians remained displaced long after he assumed office. “I have said it, and I will repeat it that after one year to 18 months in office, if any Nigerian remains in an IDP camp, we have failed,” he declared. Obi, who said he was familiar with the security challenges confronting communities in Plateau State, cited his visits to Bokkos, Mangu and Barkin Ladi as evidence of his understanding of the plight of affected residents. “No other presidential candidate has been to Bokkos, Mangu, and Barkin Ladi, so I know the pain that people are going through,” he said. He also expressed confidence that a joint administration with former Kano State Governor Rabiu Kwankwaso as vice-president would tackle kidnapping and insecurity across the country. “Let me assure you that with Kwankwaso and I as the president and vice president of this country, nobody will kidnap school children and go into the bush,” Obi said. item.title: Brazil Electoral Court Fines Meta $1.3mn In Lula-Bolsonaro Spat
item.description: Brazil’s electoral court ruled Tuesday that Meta had to pay a fine of about $1.3 million for failing to comply with court orders after President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva alleged the tech giant tipped the scales toward his rival, Flávio Bolsonaro, during the latest presidential election. Leftist leader Lula had accused Meta of “algorithmic manipulation” favoring Bolsonaro in the run-up to the October 25 runoff vote, in which he surprisingly prevailed despite coming in second during the first-round ballot. Brazil’s President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva gestures during a meeting of the National Council for the Industrialisation of Critical and Strategic Minerals at the Planalto Palace in Brasília on November 5, 2026. (Photo by Evaristo Sa / AFP) | Evaristo Sa / AFP The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) unanimously ruled to impose a fine of 7.5 million reais (around $1.3 million) on Meta, the parent company of Facebook, WhatsApp and Telegram, finding the company missed deadlines and lacked transparency in its investigation. However, the court’s reporting judge Marco Aurelio said the judicial body had not found evidence of any “deliberate action to skew the election.” This illustration photograph shows the Brazilian flag displayed on a smartphone screen in front of a screen displaying the logo of US technology company Meta in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, on October 19, 2026. Photo by MAURO PIMENTEL / AFP Meta had denied the accusations but acknowledged that some of Lula’s campaign ads had been mistakenly deactivated due to technical errors. “We are going to have to regulate them,” Lula said of social media companies after his electoral victory. After refusing to acknowledge his loss in the runoff, Flavio Bolsonaro fled Brazil to the United States amid an ongoing investigation into him for alleged money laundering. item.title: Tinubu: Anambra RHA mobilises 143,000 vote canvassers
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu The Renewed Hope Ambassadors (RHA) in Anambra State have mobilised no fewer than 143,000 vote canvassers across the state’s 5,720 polling units to campaign for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general elections. The state coordinator of RHA, Chief Okey Ezenwa, disclosed this during a meeting of the organisation’s zonal and local government coordinators. Ezenwa said each polling unit had 25 canvassers prepared to drive grassroots mobilisation for Tinubu’s re-election. “The Anambra State chapter of RHA is fully prepared for the 16 January 2027 presidential election. Our coordinators are fully on ground in the 21 Local Government Areas and the 326 wards,” he said. He disclosed that an 11-member local government committee and a 10-member ward steering committee had also been established to strengthen the organisation’s coordination and mobilisation efforts. According to him, the meeting resolved to convene a separate meeting with all APC National Assembly and State Assembly candidates in Anambra to agree on a clear strategic direction, particularly amid concerns over the perceived inactivity of the party’s state chapter. Ezenwa reaffirmed that the RHA would serve as a major political structure supporting APC candidates in the presidential, National Assembly and State Assembly elections. He also directed zonal, local government and ward coordinators to intensify grassroots mobilisation for Tinubu’s re-election. The RHA coordinator expressed the organisation’s commitment to mobilising support for the successful conduct of the forthcoming presidential campaign rallies in the state. He commended the Director-General of RHA and Governor of Imo State, Hope Uzodimma, for his efforts in mobilising support for President Tinubu across the country. item.title: DR Congo Ebola outbreak exceeds 11,000 cases
item.description: The Democratic Republic of Congo’s worst-ever outbreak of Ebola has now reached more than 11,000 confirmed cases, official Congolese figures showed on Wednesday, as armed conflict hampers the response. The 17th outbreak of the virus in the DRC’s history was officially declared in May but experts believe it emerged weeks or even months earlier. It has infected 11,042 people in the DRC and caused 5,387 deaths, according to the National Institute of Public Health. Around 2,990 people have recovered from Ebola, which is transmitted through contact with bodily fluids and causes severe hemorrhagic fever. Ebola has killed more than 15,000 people in Africa over the last 50 years. The worst outbreak previously recorded in the DRC killed nearly 2,300 people out of 3,500 cases between 2018 and 2020. The latest outbreak began in northeastern Ituri province and has since spread to seven other provinces, with most cases concentrated in Ituri and North Kivu. Cases have also been reported in Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria. No approved vaccines or treatments exist currently for the Bundibugyo species of Ebola behind the latest outbreak. Last month, the World Health Organization announced that Ervebo, a vaccine approved for use against the more common Zaire strain of Ebola, would be put through a full human trial in the DRC to see if it offered any cross-protection against Bundibugyo. Security in eastern DRC is another challenge in fighting the health crisis. Ituri province is one of the most volatile and clashes between armed groups and violence against health workers regularly occur. A health centre treating Ebola patients was set on fire on Sunday by youths in Lolwa in Ituri province, health authorities said. Clashes between local militia on the same day temporarily suspended the health response in the area of Fataki, according to the UN. Islamic State-affiliated rebels from the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) have carried out deadly attacks in several areas of Ituri, Haut-Uele and North Kivu in recent days, local and security sources said. item.title: ADC cannot stop Tinubu, APC will win all 36 states — Adeyeye
item.description: By Rotimi Ojomoyela ADO-EKITI — The Chairman of the Nigerian Ports Authority, Senator Dayo Adeyeye, has dismissed the African Democratic Congress (ADC) as a serious threat to President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027, predicting that the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) will win all 36 states. Adeyeye, who is also the National Chairman of the South-West Agenda for Asiwaju (SWAGA), said the ADC lacked the political structure, grassroots influence and electoral strength to challenge the ruling party. He also questioned the political strength of the ADC’s presidential candidate, former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, alleging that he lacked sufficient support even in his home state of Adamawa. Adeyeye spoke with journalists in Ado-Ekiti on Wednesday while assessing the political landscape ahead of the 2027 general election. He dismissed suggestions that the APC was apprehensive about the opposition, describing such claims as unfounded. According to him, the ADC has yet to demonstrate sufficient political strength at the state and National Assembly levels to pose a credible challenge to the ruling party. “How can the APC be afraid of anything with the political atmosphere we have now? I said over three months ago that President Tinubu was likely to win all the 36 states, and I am becoming increasingly convinced that it will happen. “ADC is a party without a governor in any of the 36 states. How many members does it have in the National Assembly? How many state assemblies does it control? You cannot compare a party without a demonstrable political structure with the APC,” he said. The former senator argued that Atiku’s presidential ambition was further weakened by what he described as inadequate political backing in Adamawa State. He alleged that neither the state governor nor prominent political figures in Adamawa had demonstrated substantial support for the former vice-president. “Atiku is from Adamawa, but the governor of his state is not supporting him. The legislature in the state has not witnessed any significant movement to the ADC. How do you intend to challenge and defeat an incumbent president when you cannot establish a formidable political base in your own state?” he asked. Adeyeye said SWAGA was established to consolidate Tinubu’s political base in the South-West, stressing that strong support at home was essential for any presidential candidate seeking national acceptance. He maintained that Tinubu had built a formidable political foundation across the South-West, adding that the president’s support base had continued to expand beyond the region. On the economy, Adeyeye acknowledged the hardship facing Nigerians but argued that the removal of fuel subsidy and the unification of the foreign exchange market had prevented the country from sliding into a deeper economic crisis. item.title: Customs intercepts six pangolins, two die in Oyo
item.description: By Godwin Oritse The Federal Operations Unit (FOU), Zone ‘A’, of the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) has intercepted six pangolins at Eruwa-Oni in Oyo State in a renewed crackdown on the illegal trafficking of endangered wildlife species. The interception, which took place at about 3 a.m. on Sunday, November 8, 2026, followed an intelligence-led patrol by Customs operatives. The suspected traffickers reportedly abandoned the animals and fled upon sighting the patrol team. The six pangolins were recovered alive and transported to the Unit’s headquarters in Ikeja, Lagos. However, two died shortly after arrival, leaving four surviving animals. The Customs Service subsequently handed over the four surviving pangolins and the carcasses of the two dead animals to relevant wildlife authorities for documentation and further necessary action. The handover was conducted by the Deputy Comptroller in charge of Enforcement, DC A.O. Oguntuase, on behalf of the Comptroller of FOU Zone ‘A’, Lagos. The Unit reiterated that protecting endangered species was a shared responsibility and urged members of the public to provide credible and timely information to assist law enforcement agencies in identifying and apprehending those involved in the illegal capture, possession, transportation and trafficking of protected wildlife. It also reaffirmed its commitment to suppressing smuggling and other forms of illicit trade, while strengthening collaboration with relevant agencies to protect Nigeria’s natural heritage. item.title: Awujale palace not under siege – Ogun police
item.description: The Police Command in Ogun has dismissed reports alleging that the Awujale Palace in Ijebu-Ode was under siege by thugs and miscreants. This is contained in a statement issued by DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi, the command’s spokesperson in Abeokuta on Wednesday. According to Babaseyi, the deployment is a preventive security measure aimed at safeguarding lives and property and preventing any breakdown of public peace. He added that an Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) was deployed to supervise and coordinate the security arrangement at the palace. The police spokesperson also clarified that one person had been invited following a written petition containing allegations against him. According to him, the person honoured the invitation, was questioned over the allegations and subsequently released on self-recognisance, while investigations continued. Babaseyi stressed that the invitation was part of a legitimate investigative process and should not be interpreted as an indication of guilt. He reiterated the command’s commitment to professionalism, impartiality, the rule of law and respect for the rights of all individuals. “Members of the public should remain calm, disregard misleading reports and avoid circulating unverified information capable of creating tension or disturbing public peace. “The command is committed to protecting lives and property, maintaining public order and enforcing the law impartially across the state,” he said. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the Awujale stool became vacant in July 2025, following the death of Oba Sikiru Adetona at 91, after 65 years reign. item.title: Fossil Fuels ‘Must Go The Way Of The Dinosaurs’, UN Chief Tells World Leaders At COP31
item.description: UN chief Antonio Guterres on Wednesday accused oil and gas interests of blocking action on climate change and urged world leaders at COP31 to “end the fossil fuel addiction”. “Fossil fuels must go the way of the dinosaurs, but that won’t happen on its own. The dinosaurs did not have a lobby, but fossil fuels do,” Guterres said in Turkey at his final UN climate summit as secretary-general. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres railed against the oil and gas lobby on Wednesday, urging world leaders to “end the fossil fuel addiction” at a climate summit missing several prominent figures. The two-week COP31 talks kicked off in Turkey earlier this week with governments under pressure to tackle climate change after a year of searing heatwaves and wildfires in Europe, and deadly floods in Nepal. “The brutal truth is that the climate crisis is outrunning us,” Guterres told dozens of world leaders assembled at a sprawling expo centre in the Mediterranean city of Antalya. This handout photograph taken and released by Turkish Presidency Press Office on November 10, 2026, shows Turkey’s President Recep Tayyip Erdogan (C,R) meeting with UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres (C,L) during the COP31 UN Climate Change Conference in Antalya. But few major breakthroughs are anticipated at the COP31 negotiations, which run until November 20, as countries grapple with an oil price shock and geopolitical tensions fuelled by the US war with Iran and Russia’s conflict in Ukraine. Since agreeing in 2023 for the first time to transition away from fossil fuels — the main driver of climate change — nations have struggled to advance that goal at the annual COP conferences. “Fossil fuel interests keep making a killing, while killing our planet,” Guterres said, urging governments to tax the windfall profits of oil companies. “Fossil fuels must go the way of the dinosaurs, but that won’t happen on its own. The dinosaurs did not have a lobby, but fossil fuels do,” he said. “Their strategy is simple: Distort the science. Delay the policy. Delay the action. Delay the accountability. It’s time to kick the habit –- and end the fossil fuel addiction,” he said to applause. Swedish activist Greta Thunberg arrives at the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, on November 10, 2026. Global fossil fuel emissions are projected to fall slightly in 2026 due to the expansion of renewable energy and the oil price shock sparked by the Iran war, researchers said Tuesday. Guterres, who has made the fight against climate change a central issue since taking office in 2017, is attending his last COP before his term ends in December. Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Iran’s Masoud Pezeshkian are among the leaders due to speak during the “high-level segment” taking place on Wednesday and Thursday. item.title: El Nino Fuels Indonesia Fire Outbreak, Destroys 2.88 Million Hectares – Report
item.description: Fires in Indonesia driven partly by a strong El Nino have burned through 2.88 million hectares (7.1 million acres) so far in 2026, a monitor analysing satellite imagery told AFP on Wednesday. The burned area figure — 18 times the size of London — has increased nearly a million hectares since deforestation monitoring site Nusantara Atlas’s last update in September. Indonesia’s government has not provided official figures for areas burned since announcing 202,000 hectares had been razed by the end of July. The burning detected in analysis through the end of October is a conservative estimate, warned Nusantara Atlas founder David Gaveau, in part because smoke has obscured satellite images. But it already exceeds the full-year figure for 2019, previously the worst year on record in Nusantara Atlas data. Indonesia also experienced devastating fires in 2015, but the satellite imagery used then was different, making a direct comparison difficult. Volunteers spray water to extinguish a land fire at Terantang in Barito Kuala regency, South Kalimantan province, on November 7, 2026, following months of forest and land fires. (Photo by MUDA SAGALA / AFP) Still, the scale of destruction is clear, said Gaveau. “Basically, it’s a really bad year,” he said. The arrival of rain has brought some of the worst blazes under control, and monitoring shows the number of so-called hotspots starting to flatten or decline. But the figure for total burned area is likely to rise further given some fires are still burning, and as burn scars previously hidden by smoke become visible to satellites in coming months. Indonesia’s government previously said it needed more time to analyse data before issuing updated figures. AFP has asked for comment on the monitor’s latest data. Indonesia experiences fires every dry season, but this year’s blazes have been particularly severe in part due to an intense drought caused by the El Nino weather pattern. A firefighter sprays water to extinguish a wildfire burning organic-rich peatland, which smolders underground and releases dense smoke in Pulang Pisau Regency, in Central Kalimantan province on November 4, 2026. (Photo by REINA / AFP) Experts say the fires are also the result of decades of deforestation and the drying out of peatlands for plantations, making large swathes of land more vulnerable to flames. The fires have caused devastating local pollution that has sickened hundreds of thousands of people and sent haze into neighbouring countries, including Malaysia and Singapore. item.title: Man United close to deal with Pochettino to become next coach
item.description: Manchester United are reportedly closing in on an agreement with Mauricio Pochettino to replace Michael Carrick as head coach if the club decides to end his tenure. According to Sky Sports, the former Tottenham and Chelsea manager, who currently coaches the United States national team, is being lined up as Carrick’s potential successor, with discussions between the parties said to be at an advanced stage. Carrick reported to United’s Carrington training ground at around 7:45 am on Wednesday, with uncertainty continuing over his future at Old Trafford. The club’s hierarchy is expected to discuss his position at a meeting in Monaco on Wednesday, where chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are scheduled to meet minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe. The meeting was initially arranged to review United’s performances this season, but Carrick’s position is now expected to feature prominently following the club’s disappointing start to the campaign. Berrada and Wilcox are expected to present their recommendations to Ratcliffe, who oversees football operations at the club, before a final decision is reached on the head coach’s future. Sky Sports News understands that United would have to pay approximately £7m to release Pochettino from his recently signed contract with the United States national team, although the financial requirement is not considered an obstacle to the proposed appointment. Pochettino is reportedly prepared to take over if United decide to make a change, although he is currently scheduled to lead the United States against Haiti on Saturday. Meanwhile, former United captain Roy Keane has criticised Carrick’s leadership following the club’s recent performances. Keane said the under-pressure manager “talks a lot but doesn’t say much” and needs to “get moving” on improving the team after United’s late 4-4 draw against Aston Villa. United’s struggles have increased scrutiny on Carrick, with the club’s management now considering a potential change in the dugout. item.title: FG Commissions Three CNG Facilities In Kano
item.description: The Federal Government has commissioned three Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) infrastructure facilities in Kano State, as part of efforts to expand access to cleaner and cheaper energy and reduce transportation costs. The facilities, developed by Rolling Energy Limited with support from the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund (MDGIF), comprise a 300,000-standard cubic metres per day Liquefied Compressed Natural Gas (LCNG) distribution hub and a retail station at Tamburawa, Dawakin Kudu Local Government Area, as well as a 21,000-standard cubic metres per day LCNG daughter and retail station at Hotoro, Tarauni LGA. Speaking at the commissioning ceremony, the Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Gas), Ekperikpe Ekpo, said the projects represented the Federal Government’s commitment to translating Nigeria’s abundant gas resources into tangible economic benefits for citizens. Ekpo, who was represented by a senior government official, said the facilities would strengthen gas distribution, deepen penetration in Kano and neighbouring communities, support businesses and transportation, and create new economic opportunities. He said the Tamburawa hub would provide integrated LNG storage, regasification and CNG distribution services, including the capacity to supply daughter stations, while the retail outlets would ensure that the product reached consumers directly. “Together, these three facilities demonstrate the complete philosophy of our domestic gas agenda: building the infrastructure to receive and distribute gas, while simultaneously creating the last-mile outlets that make the product accessible to Nigerians,” he said. Ekpo during the opening of two CNG daughter stations capable of dispensing CNG to more than 2,500 vehicles and 50 trucks daily in Kano, on Tuesday, November 10, 2026. The minister said the projects aligned with President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, which, according to him, seeks to move the country from policy formulation to the delivery of critical infrastructure. “His charge to us is clear: we must move from policies to projects, from plans to infrastructure, and from gas reserves beneath our soil to affordable energy that actually reaches our homes, businesses, industries and transportation systems,” he said. Ekpo added that government was determined to mobilise private sector investment to accelerate the development of the country’s gas infrastructure. He commended Rolling Energy, MDGIF, regulators, investors and other technical partners for their contributions to the projects. Also speaking, the Executive Chairman of the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles, Barr. Ismaeel Ahmed, said the expansion of CNG infrastructure across the country showed that investments in the sector were yielding results. item.title: Many terrorists neutralised as military sustains pressure on enclaves
item.description: Scores of terrorists have been neutralised across different communities in the Northern region of the country following the pressure sustained in their enclaves by the troops of the Nigerian military. The troops, in different operations sustained pressure on the criminals and dismantled criminal networks with a view to protecting lives and property, and restoring lasting peace and security across the country. Daily Trust reports that the development was in line with the commitment of the Armed Forces of Nigeria under the leadership of General Olufemi Olatunbosun Oluyede. The four-star general, has at different fora maintained that he would continue to ensure that all law-abiding Nigerians, particularly those in the Northern Nigeria sleep with their two eyes closed. Updating Nigerians on the efforts being made to restore peace across the country, the Director, Defence Media Operations, Major-General Michael Onoja disclosed that consistent efforts were made to deny terrorists, kidnappers, gunrunners and other criminal groups’ freedom of action between October 30th and November 5th, 2026. Terrorists suffer heavy losses in Northeast Checks showed that in the North East geopolitical zone, troops of Operation HADIN KAI inflicted heavy losses on terrorists who attempted to strike at troops’ locations in Borno and Yobe States. Subsequently, troops pressed home the advantage with clearance operations and a wave of arrests. On the night of October 29th, 2026, terrorists approached Buni Yadi in Gujba LGA of Yobe State, from the Timbuktu Triangle axis. However, troops countered the attack and subsequent exploitation on 30 October 30th, 2026 discovered the bodies of 48 terrorists, along with 42 AK-47 rifles, five PKT machine guns, four general-purpose machine guns, a 60mm mortar, 105 magazines and two video cameras. The following day, troops’ operations around Apama and Jauro Bashir along the terrorists’ withdrawal route, recovered three corpses, an AK-47 rifle and 188 rounds of ammunition. The senior military officer confirmed that on the same day, terrorists also attempted to infiltrate a troops’ location at Bitta in Gwoza LGA of Borno State but were forced to retreat. He added, “Exploitation at first light recovered the bodies of seven terrorists, four AK-47 rifles, an RPG tube, four RPG bombs, three RPG chargers, a PKM machine gun and a radio. “Troops also received several surrendered members of terrorist groups, rescued escapees and dismantled terrorist support networks across the theatre. “Between 2 – 4 November 2026, twelve terrorist fighters and family members surrendered at New Abaram Resettlement Village and Banki Junction in Bama LGA and near Ngurusoye in Gwoza LGA in Borno State.” On November 2nd, 2026, troops rescued a female abductee who had escaped from the Mandara Mountains at Hudugum, Hambagda, along the Gwoza-Limankara Road.
